lead.claim: For CP, whole-body vibration plus stretching may improve knee ROM more than ultrasound.
lead.context: Why this matters: This randomized trial compared therapeutic ultrasound and whole-body vibration as adjuncts to passive stretching in children with hemiplegic cerebral palsy.

supporting.claim: AI models show promise in rehab treatment planning, but require expert supervision.
supporting.context: Why this matters: This systematic review explored the capabilities of large language models in supporting rehabilitation treatment planning.

supporting.claim: Home-based brain-computer interface therapy may offer lasting motor gains for stroke survivors.
supporting.context: Why this matters: This retrospective observational study assessed motor status in stroke survivors using at-home BCI therapy.

supporting.claim: For obese children with flat feet, plyometrics may improve balance more than corrective exercises.
supporting.context: Why this matters: This comparative study examined the effects of plyometric versus flatfoot corrective exercises on balance and foot posture.

supporting.claim: External training load metrics describe movement, not always biological demand; use caution.
supporting.context: Why this matters: This systematic review evaluated the construct validity of external training load metrics in sport.
